title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 25-27). M is a set of 'pieces' carrying two relations. The first, <=, is an order ('is a face of'). The second, <<, is weaker, a kind of incidence or 'adherence' relation, with ML0: X <= Y implies X << Y. L is a subset of M, the 'points', originally meant to be the <<-minimal elements. For X in M, X~ = {Y in M : Y <= X}. The shadow ('ombre') of X is omb(X) = {x in L : x << X}, the set of points adherent to X, i.e. its 'closure'. The open shadow is omb(X)° = omb(X) minus the union of omb(Y) over Y < X, i.e. the points adherent to X but to no proper face, the 'open cell'. Write x <<° X for x in omb(X)°, i.e. X is minimal in X~^x = {X' <= X : x << X'}. ML1 says two faces of X adherent to x have a common face adherent to x, an Inf-type condition. Lemma 1 (p. 25) says that, given ML1 and ML2, the following are equivalent: X <= Y; X << Y; omb X is contained in omb Y; omb(X)° is contained in omb(Y); omb(X)° meets omb(Y).

This page.
(1) Corollary: if omb(X)° meets omb(Y)°, then X = Y. Lemma 1 applied both ways gives X <= Y and Y <= X, then antisymmetry. So the open cells of distinct pieces are disjoint.
(2) Two axioms are bracketed together and labelled At_L 1. ML2: every open shadow is nonempty, i.e. every piece has an 'interior point'. ML3: for each X, the omb(Y)° with Y <= X cover omb(X). That is, for each x << X there is Y <= X with x <<° Y.
(3) Marginal remark: ML2 and ML3 are a form of At_M 4-). Together they say that omb(X) is partitioned by the open cells of the faces of X. This is the combinatorial content of a stratification satisfying the frontier condition: closure of a stratum = disjoint union of the strata of its faces, each nonempty.
(4) NB: by the corollary the Y in ML3 is unique. Moreover, if Y' <= X and x << Y', then x lies in omb(Y)° and in omb(Y'), so Y <= Y' by Lemma 1. Hence Y is the smallest element of X~^x, the 'carrier' or support cell of x in X.
(5) A crossed-out start of 'Lemme 2' leads to a methodological remark. So far nothing has used that L consists of the <<-minimal elements; one could take any L satisfying ML2 and ML3. Taking L = M:
- ML2 becomes 'trivial', since X itself should lie in its own open shadow.
- ML3 becomes the statement that for every Z << X there is Y <= X with Z <<° Y. This is the axiom At_M 4-) of p. 6.
- But ML1 would then have to be generalized, replacing the point x by an arbitrary piece Z.
(6) Grothendieck suggests deriving the M-level statement from the L-level axioms (ML2, ML3, generalized ML1). Given Z << X, pick an interior point x <<° Z (ML2). Take the unique Y <= X with x <<° Y (ML3). Then show Z <<° Y. The key step: any Y' <= X with Z << Y' should be forced to be >= Y, so the carrier of x is also the carrier of Z.
The next page carries this out as Lemma 2, explicitly assuming ML1 in generalized form, and proves that for x <<° Z << X', x <<° X' iff Z <<° X'. This yields At_M 4 a).

Purpose: an axiomatic, point-set-free (poset-plus-incidence) description of tame stratified or cellular spaces in the 1986 'Analysis situs' project. A structure on pieces (M, <=, <<) is to be compatible with a set of points L via shadows, deriving properties at the level of pieces from properties at the level of points.
errors: NB paragraph: the manuscript writes that Y' is the smallest element of X~^x. The argument actually shows Y <= Y' for every such Y', so it is Y, the carrier from ML3, that is the smallest; Y' is a slip.
The corollary silently needs antisymmetry of <= (X <= Y and Y <= X imply X = Y). It also inherits Lemma 1's dependence on ML1 and ML2, but ML2 is only formally stated on this page.
'If L = M, ML2 is trivial' requires X <<° X. That needs X << X' <= X to imply X' = X, i.e. some antisymmetry linking << with <=, which is not among the stated axioms ML0-ML1.

Final lines: 'si x << Y <= X, alors Z <= Y' is unjustified as written. What can be expected (and what p. 27 proves, using generalized ML1) is Z << Y; the passage is visibly tentative ('il devrait être possible').

ideas.what: Shadow omb(X) and open shadow omb(X)° of a piece in a set of points; x <<° X as 'x lies in the open cell of X'
ideas.modern_name: closure / open cell of a stratum in a face poset; carrier (support) cell of a point
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (abstract cell complexes: Tucker, Lefschetz 1940s; stratification theory: Whitney, Thom)

ideas.what: ML2 + ML3: the open cells of the faces of X partition omb(X), each nonempty; the corollary gives disjointness
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition / poset-stratified space, closure of a stratum = union of the strata below
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom/Mather (frontier condition); poset-stratified spaces in Lurie, Higher Algebra A.5
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame topology and stratified structures, but not these axioms

ideas.what: Uniqueness and minimality of the carrier: the unique Y with x <<° Y is the smallest face of X adherent to x
ideas.modern_name: carrier of a point in a regular cell complex

ideas.what: Methodological point: the axioms need not use that L consists of <<-minimal elements; with L = M they become the M-level axiom At_M 4-); program to derive M-level axioms from point-level ones via ML1 generalized to arbitrary pieces Z
ideas.modern_name: comparing an incidence structure on pieces with its point realization (cf. Alexandrov topology on face posets, specialization order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific standard credit; cf. P. S. Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies

missed.claim: An abstract two-relation axiomatics (<= for faces, << for adherence) for 'analysis situs' of tame stratified objects. The axioms are formulated through shadows of pieces on a set of points, with a deliberate attempt to separate point-level axioms (ML1-3 for L) from piece-level ones (At_M). This is part of Grothendieck's never-published attempt to found tame topology combinatorially.
missed.quote: On ne voit pas jusqu'ici pourquoi utiliser la définition des sous-ensembles L de M, comme formé d'él. minimaux pour <<
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to current axiomatics of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, conically stratified spaces, o-minimal cell decompositions). It documents what combinatorial frontier-type axioms Grothendieck considered basic in 1986, but it reinvents rather standard face-poset material.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary order-theoretic bookkeeping: disjointness and partition of open cells, and the carrier of a point. The mathematics is routine. Its interest is historical, as a trace of the unpublished 1986 tame-topology axiomatics; nothing here would surprise a specialist mathematically.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note reads roughly 'At_M 4-) forme de ML2 et ML3 ... signifient que les omb(Y)° forment une partition de [omb] X'. The partition is of omb(X), not X itself.
The label 'AtL1' with a vertical bar groups ML2 and ML3 as an axiom At_L 1, the L-level analogue of the At_M axioms.
NB: the conclusion should read that Y (not Y') is the smallest element of X~^x. The manuscript has Y', apparently a slip.
'pourrions quand même supposer' is better read as 'pourrait-on quand même supposer'.

Near the end: 'il y a des points x in L, x <<° Z (ML2), et l'unique Y in X~ tel que x <<° Y (ML3), et il faudrait prouver que Z <<° Y'. The marginal '(ML3)' over 'L'idée est' is likely '(ML2)', since the existence of points x <<° Z is ML2.
